data.title: From anti-war physicist to AI power broker, Amodei takes his safety approach public
data.description:
By Aditya Soni and Jeffrey Dastin

Nov 19 (Reuters) - Long before Dario Amodei butted heads with the Pentagon over whether the US military could use Anthropic's models for mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons, he was fighting another battle.

At the California Institute of Technology in 2003, Amodei called on his classmates to join him in protesting the US invasion of Iraq, writing in an op-ed that citizen-scientists should not be "reduced to amoral technicians who run the machines of war."

On Thursday, as 43-year-old Amodei led his startup to an IPO that raised a record $81 billion and valued it at about $1.5 trillion, the listing cemented his transformation from an idealistic physics student into one of the most powerful custodians of the AI age.

"We will not bend to either business nor political pressure," Amodei said at the Nasdaq on Thursday in New York. "Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing."

Amodei has spent much of his ascent emphasizing curbs on a technology whose extraordinary potential he has devoted his career to unlocking, and has now made his company one of the most valuable on Wall Street. Even as Anthropic prepared for its debut, Amodei penned a nearly 4,000-word essay in September, warning how AI's advances could outpace human control and urging a slowdown in development.

Days later, Anthropic released a new version of one of its most powerful models in a challenge to rival OpenAI, where he worked before quitting over differences related to AI safety.

In that essay, Amodei denied any contradiction between his quest for safe AI and Anthropic's race to develop the most powerful models.

"I have grappled with this duality of risk and benefit since the beginning of Anthropic," he wrote. "Not building the technology deprives humanity of benefits or simply places AI in the hands of authoritarian powers, while building it too fast is reckless."

Anthropic was a commercially viable company spurring a safety "race to the top," he said.

This approach has drawn criticism both from advocates of greater safety measures and from Silicon Valley executives who have warned against slowing down innovation, such as Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang. Amodei's determination to impose some limits on AI also earned him enemies in Washington, culminating in an extraordinary showdown with the Trump administration early this year. 

Following a meeting between Amodei and US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, the government set a deadline for Anthropic to accept the military's contract terms, which the company rejected. That led to a government blacklist of its technology that the Claude maker challenged in court.

Anthropic declined to comment for this story. 

Anthropic shares rose sharply on their first day of trading, debuting at $111.50, 34% higher than the $83 IPO price. 

THE PRICE OF CAUTION

Though the IPO was expected to mint thousands of paper millionaires, Amodei has said the company's safety focus has come at a cost.

Last month he responded to a post on X that challenged Anthropic's safety record and criticized a change to its pledge around halting AI development if it cannot minimize risks. Amodei said the company had "likely sacrificed a significant chunk of a several-month model lead" by delaying the release of its powerful Mythos models over hacking risks and initially limiting access to cybersecurity defenders.

Anthropic is spending billions of dollars on computing capacity each year, making it harder as a publicly traded company - albeit one where its seven co-founders or a trust wield voting control on key matters - to justify slowing model development as shareholders seek returns.

In its IPO filing, though, the company noted that its corporate setup could lead to decisions that "may conflict with short-, medium-, or long-term financial interests and business performance," and said it had paused training of a next-generation ‌flagship AI model for more than a month over security concerns.

LESSONS FROM THE ATOM BOMB

Dario Amodei and his sister and co-founder Daniela grew up in San Francisco's Mission District, just a few miles from the spot where Anthropic would eventually occupy a glass tower with Silicon Valley perks such as a gourmet espresso bar.

He was voted "most likely to succeed" by his eighth-grade classmates, a yearbook snippet shows, and admitted to San Francisco's selective Lowell public high school. He went to Caltech before transferring to Stanford, and then attended Princeton, where he earned a PhD focusing on biophysics and computational neuroscience.

After his father's death from hepatitis C about two decades ago - a few years before medical advances dramatically improved survival rates - Amodei pursued artificial intelligence that could accelerate medicine. In a podcast, talking about his dad's illness, Amodei pushed back against criticism that he was simply an AI "doomer."

Amodei's preoccupation with AI safety has influenced his management style.

Daniela Amodei has oversight of day-to-day operations at the company, while Dario Amodei devotes almost 40% of his time to framing the culture and vision of Anthropic through essays and fortnightly company-wide meetings that employees have dubbed "Dario Vision Quests."

"Operationally, the buck stops with her," a former employee said of Anthropic President Daniela Amodei. "Strategically, it stops with him."

Dario Amodei said in a Bloomberg interview published in June that he had only one direct report, calling the structure "incredibly freeing."

One of his favorite books is "The Making of the Atomic Bomb," written by Richard Rhodes. Talking about Robert Oppenheimer, the bomb's architect, Amodei said: "In some ways I actually see Oppenheimer as a failure case, as what should not happen."

(Reporting by Aditya Soni in Bengaluru and Jeffrey Dastin in San Francisco; Writing by Sayantani Ghosh; Editing by David Gaffen)

data.title: RADIN Health Unveils RADINA™, the Autonomous AI Ecosystem for Imaging, at RSNA 2026
data.description:
One autonomous AI platform guiding every patient from referral to follow-up, automating repetitive work, connecting workflows, and helping imaging organizations scale without adding administrative complexity.

SHERIDAN, Wyo., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- RADIN Health today announced RADINA, a next-generation AI platform designed to automate and orchestrate imaging workflows across the entire patient journey. Scheduled to be officially unveiled at RSNA 2026, RADINA serves as the AI layer behind RADIN™, connecting operational, clinical, and patient-facing workflows into a single intelligent ecosystem.

Imaging organizations face continued pressure from workforce shortages, rising labor costs, increasing patient volumes, reimbursement cuts, and growing compliance requirements. While healthcare software has digitized many imaging processes, organizations still rely heavily on staff to coordinate referrals, insurance verification, prior authorizations, scheduling, patient communications, reporting workflows, and follow-up management.

"Healthcare doesn't need more dashboards, more queues, or more disconnected applications," said Dr. Alejandro Bugnone, Chief Executive Officer of RADIN Health. "It needs systems that understand what should happen next and can make it happen. RADINA was built to automate repetitive work, eliminate unnecessary handoffs, and help imaging organizations scale without increasing administrative complexity."

Unlike traditional workflow tools that automate individual tasks, RADINA continuously evaluates the state of each patient's journey and determines the next action required to move care forward. The platform follows patients from referral intake through scheduling, authorization, imaging, reporting, and follow-up management while escalating exceptions to staff when human judgment is required.

RADINA moves beyond traditional workflow automation by coordinating the next best action across the imaging journey and executing routine operational tasks from referral intake through follow-up. The platform was built around a simple principle: "If the system knows what has to happen next, nobody should have to remember it."

Experience the Official RADINA Launch at RSNA 2026

RSNA attendees are invited to visit RADIN Health Booth #5515 for the official launch of RADINA™ on Sunday, November 29 at 10:40 AM. Visitors will have the opportunity to meet the RADINA Concierge robot, an AI-powered digital front desk that greets patients, automates check-in, supports registration workflows, and can escort patients to their destination within an imaging center. Available as a mobile robotic assistant, self-service kiosk or tablet, RADINA Concierge demonstrates how imaging organizations can modernize patient access while reducing administrative burden and improving operational efficiency. 

RSNA 2026 attendees can also experience live demonstrations of RADINA at the RADIN Health exhibit booth #5515. Dr. Alejandro Bugnone is scheduled to speak at RSNA on Guiding the Referral-to-Follow-Up Patient Journey on November 30 from 1:00 PM to 1:20 PM at Innovation Theater, Booth 3352, and on Agentic AI with Clinical Oversight on December 1 from 12:00 PM to 12:20 PM at AI Theater, Booth 5536.

RADINA Autopilot™ - The Autonomous Imaging Workflow Engine

At the center of the platform is RADINA Autopilot™, an autonomous workflow engine that connects imaging operations into a single continuous workflow. Autopilot manages each patient's progression through the imaging process and automatically initiates the next appropriate step. It runs the entire referral-to-follow-up cycle as one workflow while engaging staff only when decisions require human oversight.

RADINA Autopilot can:

  • Process incoming referrals and orders
  • Verify insurance eligibility and medical necessity
  • Manage scheduling workflows
  • Coordinate prior authorizations
  • Engage patients through voice, chat, and digital communications
  • Send forms, perform digital check-in, and collect patient payments
  • Monitor report quality and compliance
  • Track completion of radiologist report imaging follow-up recommendations

According to RADIN Health, imaging organizations spend significant administrative time moving patients from referral to completed exam. RADINA is designed to reduce manual effort by automating routine tasks and allowing staff to focus on exceptions, patient support, and clinical coordination.

A Connected AI Ecosystem

RADINA includes AI-powered products and capabilities spanning imaging operations, radiologist productivity, quality assurance, compliance, and revenue optimization. The platform operates as a unified intelligence layer across the imaging enterprise, following the patient from referral through follow-up.

  • Conversational patient scheduling

  • Digital payment collection

  • Follow-up recommendation tracking
  • Closed-loop patient follow-up management

"RADINA represents a new generation of technology that doesn't just document work, it helps perform it," said Dipali Lohar, Chief Product Officer of RADIN Health.

The platform maintains a single workflow and timeline for every patient, enabling organizations to reduce administrative friction, minimize missed steps, improve patient engagement, and ensure follow-up recommendations are completed.

RADIN is a comprehensive cloud-native platform and intelligent workflow ecosystem for radiology and diagnostic imaging organizations. Its technology unifies enterprise imaging, RIS, PACS, SELECT workflow orchestration, dictation, intelligent worklists, clinical communications, patient engagement, analytics, compliance, and AI-powered automation within a single connected environment. Designed for hospitals, imaging centers, radiology groups, and teleradiology practices, RADIN helps healthcare organizations improve operational efficiency, clinical quality, patient access, financial performance, scalability, and care coordination across the entire imaging journey, from referral to follow-up.

Nov 19 (Reuters) - For decades, venture capital thrived on small bets that became billion-dollar companies.

Then came Anthropic, rewriting the playbook and forcing investors to write fatter checks to buy stakes at unheard-of valuations. 

The AI lab's shares began trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday at a $1.5 trillion valuation, delivering multibillion-dollar windfalls to venture investors at a moment when the industry needs fresh liquidity to fund more bets on AI companies. The stock closed at $97.17, up 17% from its IPO price of $83.

Anthropic's stock market value ended the day at about $1.3 trillion, based on its outstanding shares, or $1.8 trillion, based on its fully diluted shares.

To join the fundraising frenzy, especially at later stages, venture capital firms invested billions, tapping their own investors for additional capital through special-purpose vehicles.

MENLO, SPARK REAP BIG RETURNS

Menlo Ventures and Spark Capital emerged with some of the biggest returns by multiple. Spark Capital was the first venture capital firm to lead an Anthropic investment, in a $450 million Series C round in 2023 at a valuation of $4.5 billion. Spark general partner Yasmin Razavi, who spearheaded the investment, remains the only investor who sits on Anthropic's board.

Writing the largest check in the firm's history, early-stage firm Menlo invested over $1 billion for a stake of nearly 1.5%, according to a person familiar with the investment. At a $1.5 trillion market cap, Menlo's stake is worth over $20 billion. 

To invest beyond the capacity of its existing fund, Menlo raised a $750 million special-purpose vehicle from limited partners, a tactic that became increasingly common as funding rounds grew, given the capital needs of AI companies.

THE LATE-STAGE BETS PAID OFF

Sequoia Capital, long known for its early bets, joined a later round and still stands to earn billions of dollars.

Sequoia passed on Anthropic at lower prices. After a leadership change, it wrote its first check at the start of this year, joining a round led by Singapore's GIC and Coatue at a $380 billion post-money valuation in February. It later co-led, alongside Altimeter, Dragoneer and Greenoaks, a round at $965 billion. Sequoia has invested $3 billion in Anthropic and continued to invest more through Anthropic's IPO, signaling further conviction in the AI lab. 

Lightspeed Venture Partners, which invested more than $3 billion in Anthropic, now holds over 2% of the company, making it the largest financial investor in the company, according to two people familiar with the matter. 

The returns are possible because of the rapid rise in Anthropic's valuation and revenue. Its annualized revenue grew from about $1 billion at the start of 2025 to about $81 billion last month, as its valuation climbed from $61.5 billion in March 2025 to $965 billion in the latest private round this May.

Strategic backers, too, supply much of the unprecedented capital and computing power needed by AI labs. The combined stake of Amazon and Alphabet's Google in Anthropic is about 28.4%.  

"We're living through a very unique time of profound change happening at a higher velocity than ever before. The scale of the impact of these businesses and the breadth of market opportunities is larger than anything we've seen before. And that is going to afford investment opportunities that are larger than what we've seen in the past," said Will Griffith, a partner at Iconiq, which has invested $6.1 billion, making the fund the second-largest financial investor by ownership in Anthropic. 

(Reporting by Krystal Hu in San Francisco; Additional reporting by Noel Randewich in San Francisco; Editing by Sayantani Ghosh and Matthew Lewis)

data.title: TPG to take BILL Holdings private in $6 billion deal
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Fintech firm BILL Holdings ( BILL ) said on Thursday it will be acquired by private equity group TPG, in partnership with Corpay ( CPAY ), in an all-cash transaction valued at about $6 billion.

BILL will be acquired for $63.25 per share. The offer represents a 31% premium to the 60-day volume-weighted average share price through November 16, the last full trading day before BILL takeover talks were reported.

The company was valued at a little under $5 billion before the media reports. Its shares fell about 3.7% in after-hours trading.

Corpay ( CPAY ) will invest $1.1 billion for a roughly one-third stake in the company, with an option to buy the rest.

"We expect the transaction to be accretive to Corpay ( CPAY ) cash EPS in 2027, and the take-private transaction structure gives the company the flexibility to transform and accelerate profit growth. We have the option to buy the rest of the company in 2030," said Peter Walker, CFO of Corpay ( CPAY ).

The deal is set to close in the first half of 2027.

BILL provides cloud-based software that helps small and midsize businesses automate financial operations, including accounts payable and receivable.

Investor pressure on BILL mounted in September last year after activist investor Starboard Value disclosed an 8.5% stake and nominated four board candidates, signaling a potential proxy fight.

Around the same time, Reuters reported that activist Elliott Investment Management had also built a large stake and pushed for a sale. Facing competition from newer rivals offering cheaper alternatives, BILL was exploring a sale, Reuters had reported a year ago, citing sources.

Starboard Value, BILL's largest stockholder, agreed to vote its shares in favor of the agreement, the companies said.

Analysts say the company's improved margins following its plan to cut about 30% of its workforce earlier in the year have boosted its appeal as a takeover target.

Goldman Sachs and Qatalyst Partners are financial advisors to BILL. Barclays is exclusive financial advisor to Corpay ( CPAY ).

(Reporting by Pritam Biswas in Bengaluru; Editing by Tasim Zahid and Shinjini Ganguli)

data.title: BILL Agrees to be Acquired by TPG in Partnership with Corpay
data.description:
BILL will be acquired for $63.25 per share in an all-cash transaction, representing a fully diluted equity value of approximately $6.0 billion

SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- BILL , the intelligent finance platform trusted by nearly 500,000 businesses to manage, move, and maximize their money, today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to be acquired by TPG, a leading global alternative asset management firm, in partnership with Corpay ( CPAY ) , the Global Spend Management Company. BILL will be acquired for $63.25 per share in a cash transaction that values BILL at $6.0 billion. TPG will acquire a majority interest in BILL through TPG Capital, the firm’s U.S. and European private equity platform, and Corpay ( CPAY ) will acquire a minority interest.

The per share purchase price represents a 31% premium to the 60-day volume-weighted average price ending on November 16, the last full trading day preceding media reports that BILL was in acquisition discussions.

“This transaction marks an exciting new chapter for BILL, delivering significant, certain, and immediate value to our stockholders, while creating new opportunities to accelerate our transformation and deliver greater value to customers,” said René Lacerte, CEO and Founder of BILL. “With our new partners, we will have the resources, expertise, and strategic support to accelerate innovation, advance our AI transformation, and continue to drive the future of financial operations. We look forward to the opportunities ahead for our customers and our business.”

“BILL has built a differentiated financial operations platform that helps small and midsize businesses manage their most critical financial workflows. We have long recognized the significant opportunity at the intersection of financial technology, AI, and payments, and believe BILL is well positioned to capitalize on these trends through its scaled network, integrated technology, and deep customer relationships,” said John Flynn, Partner at TPG. “We are excited to partner with the BILL team, combining TPG’s technology investing and business-building experience with Corpay’s payments expertise to accelerate innovation and support the company's next chapter,” added Tim Millikin, Partner at TPG.

“We’re excited about the potential this agreement represents and have great respect for everything the BILL team has accomplished. We see clear opportunities to support and complement BILL’s product roadmap, platform capabilities, and the services it offers to a broader range of customers. We look forward to working with BILL to further enhance its market-leading platform to deliver greater innovation and value to customers,” said Ron Clarke, Chairman and CEO of Corpay ( CPAY ).

Transaction Details
The transaction, which was approved unanimously by the BILL Board of Directors, is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to customary closing conditions, including approval by BILL stockholders and the receipt of required regulatory approvals. There are no financing conditions to the transaction. Starboard Value, BILL's largest stockholder, and BILL’s CEO and Founder, René Lacerte, have agreed to vote their shares in favor of the agreement.

Upon the close of the transaction, Mr. Lacerte will continue to lead BILL as CEO. BILL will become a privately held company, and its common stock will no longer be listed on any public stock exchange.

Advisors
Goldman Sachs and Qatalyst Partners are serving as financial advisors to BILL, Fenwick & West LLP is serving as BILL’s legal advisor, and Joele Frank, Wilkinson Brimmer Katcher is serving as strategic communications advisor.

BofA Securities, Inc., Deutsche Bank Securities Inc., and RBC Capital Markets, LLC are serving as financial advisors to TPG. Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP is serving as legal counsel.

Barclays is serving as financial adviser to Corpay ( CPAY ). Sullivan & Cromwell LLP is serving as legal counsel.

We use AI to deliver strategic finance capabilities in one integrated platform that includes AP, AR, expenses, forecasting, procurement and more. Headquartered in San Jose, California, BILL is a trusted partner of leading U.S. financial institutions, accounting firms, and software providers. For more information, visit bill.com.

About TPG
TPG is a leading global alternative asset management firm, founded in San Francisco in 1992, with $346 billion of assets under management and investment and operational teams around the world. TPG invests across a broadly diversified set of strategies, including private equity, impact, credit, real estate, and market solutions, and our unique strategy is driven by collaboration, innovation, and inclusion. Our teams combine deep product and sector experience with broad capabilities and expertise to develop differentiated insights and add value for our fund investors, portfolio companies, management teams, and communities.

About Corpay ( CPAY )
Corpay ( CPAY ) , the Global Spend Management Company, is an S&P 500 company with three primary B2B solution sets. Spend Management, provides corporate and virtual card programs and AP automation solutions. Cross-Border, helps businesses manage foreign-currency exposure and provides global multi-currency account solutions. Vehicle Solutions, controls fuel, tolls, parking and related vehicle spend. With Corpay ( CPAY ), the more a business controls, the less it spends. To learn more, visit corpay.com.
